Counsel for Respondent :- A.S.G.I.,C.S.C.,Vivek Kumar Singh
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Manish Kumar Nigam,J.
1.

The prayer made in the instant petition is for a direction to respondent no. 2 to decide the
representation of the petitioner dated 09.07.2024 and not to release compensation amount in
favour of any person in respect of acquired land bearing Gata No. 169 Khasra No. 503 area 1.552
hectare.
2.  The petitioner claims that he and his brothers were duped in executing sale deed on 14.10.2011 in favour of the private respondents.

The petitioner has already instituted a suit bearing No. 138 of Raza Mohammad vs Union Of India And 6 Others on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63835262/
1 2014 against the private respondents for cancellation of sale deed and same is pending.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The aforesaid land was acquired under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and award was declared in respect of the said land on 23.06.2023.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The petitioner has filed an application before respondent no. 2 praying that the compensation amount may not be disbursed in favour of the private respondents in view of the pendency of civil suit.
4. Respondent no. 2 has furnished written instructions and the same is taken on record.
According to it, respondent no. 2 after receipt of the representation from the petitioner has fixed several dates for deciding the same.

The next date now fixed is 20.08.2024.
5.
It is apparent from the pleadings and the submissions made that the petitioner is disputing the entitlement of the private respondents to receive compensation for the acquired land.
6. In our opinion, the said dispute can only be decided as per the provisions of Section 64 and Section 76 of the Act by seeking reference to the Authority.

7. Section 77(2) contemplates that in case there is any dispute relating to the title to receive the compensation, the Collector shall deposit the amount of compensation with the authority to which reference under Section 64 would be submitted.
8. We find that the petitioner has not filed any proper application before respondent no. 2 for referring the dispute to the authority.

9. Consequently, we dispose of the instant petition with liberty to the petitioner to move proper application in this behalf, if so advised and in which event, respondent no. 2 will proceed in the manner provided under the law.
10. This order has been passed in presence of Shri Vivek Kumar Singh, learned counsel for respondent no. 1.
